result.summary:
Independently re-derived every check against docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-031.md, not against TEST-DESIGNER's own result.summary.

AC coverage: all 7 acceptance criteria (requirements.yaml REQ-031, verified by direct read) each map to at least one concrete, mechanically-followable verification case -- AC1/AC7/File1-AC1 piggyback, AC2/File2-AC2, AC3/File2-AC3 sub-cases A+B, AC4/File1-AC4 three-run sequence, AC5/File2-AC5 decline+accept, AC6/File2-AC6 static grep, plus S3 exploit (3 sub-attacks) and the stale-reply field-match case. No TODO anywhere in the document (full read, line 1-481). Every case names an exact function/handler, exact fixture values, and an exact expected result -- no case relies on judgment ('check it looks right').

Hard checks specifically re-derived against real code, not trusted from the spec's prose:
- AC2 duplicate-INSERT case: confirmed it is a raw `db.insert(schema.feedback).values(...)` call, genuinely bypassing writeFeedbackNps's own `.onConflictDoUpdate(...)` (domain/feedback.ts:107-113) -- this is a different code path, not a second call through the app's upsert (which would silently no-op and never touch the DB constraint). Confirmed the DB side actually enforces this: apps/bot/drizzle/0006_smiling_leader.sql creates `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_feedback_registration_id ... USING btree (registration_id)` -- a genuine unique constraint the raw insert will collide with, Postgres code 23505.
- AC4 arithmetic: hand-recomputed selectRegistrationsForFeedbackReminder's actual window (scheduler/feedbackJobs.ts:70-100) against the spec's three evaluationTimes. Run1 (evaluationTime24 = endsAt+24h05m): windowEnd=endsAt+5m, windowStart=endsAt-1h55m -- endsAt<=windowEnd true, endsAt>windowStart true -> selected, matches spec. Run3 (evaluationTime48 = endsAt+48h05m): windowEnd=endsAt+24h05m, windowStart=endsAt+22h05m -- endsAt<=windowEnd true, endsAt>windowStart FALSE (endsAt is earlier than windowStart, not later) -> excluded, matches spec's stated conclusion. The spec's own intermediate substitution ('windowEnd = endsAt+24h... = endsAt+22h') is off by the 5-minute offset baked into the fixture times, but the sign/conclusion (condition is false, registration excluded at T+48h) is correct when computed precisely -- this is a cosmetic imprecision in the write-up, not a wrong test expectation, and does not affect the pass/fail assertions the actual test code will make.
- Stale-reply case: traced against handlers/feedback.ts:267's actual gate (`step.kind !== "feedback-field" || step.field === "nps" || step.field !== parsed.field`). The spec's constructed scenario (reply to the old `liked` prompt while the flow's current step.field is `improve`) produces parsed.field="liked" !== step.field="improve", triggering the gate and returning before any write -- this is exactly the case CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's step-01b handoff identified as the design's original bug (a reply to a superseded prompt for a DIFFERENT, still-valid sibling field being misattributed to the currently-expected field), and the rework fixed it with this exact third clause. The spec's case is not a weaker variant -- it reproduces the precise walkthrough from the validator's FAIL finding.
- AC5 accept-case fixture: confirmed present as a full separate `it(...)` (not merely mentioned in prose) -- 'Accept case, separate fixture (user V, distinct from U)'. Confirmed against domain/feedback.ts's determineFeedbackFlowStep that the gate is genuinely `broadcastOptInAskedAt === null`, never `broadcastOptIn`'s value -- matching step-01b's own AC5 finding and making the accept-case fixture the only one of the two that can catch a regression to gating on the answer value instead.
- S3 three sub-attacks: confirmed each targets a distinct handler/entry point by line number -- NPS callback ownership check at handlers/feedback.ts:144, broadcast callback at :200, text-reply at :254 -- matching SECURITY-REVIEWER's step-02c independent trace of the same three line numbers. Genuinely three distinct forgery attempts, not three variations of one.
- AC6 static grep vocabulary (`talk|speaker|want to speak`, case-insensitive) is sufficient: it would catch a re-introduction of the excluded 'want to speak at a future event?' question (PRD FR-8's D2/Release-3 element) by any of the vocabulary a real implementation would need (a catalog key, a column, a UI label) -- confirmed the file list matches every file this requirement actually touched (schema.ts, domain/feedback.ts, handlers/feedback.ts, scheduler/feedbackJobs.ts, i18n files).
- tg_id ranges: ran `grep -rn "nextTgId = " apps/bot/src` myself -- confirmed the spec's claimed existing-range list (800M/900M/920M/940M/941M/942M x2/943M/950M x2/960M/970M/980M/990M/1000000900) matches the actual grep output exactly, and 993_000_000/994_000_000 do not collide with any of them.
- AC7: confirmed domain/notification.ts:118 gates the `broadcastOptIn` read strictly inside the `classification === "marketing"` branch (with an explicit comment 'never reads broadcastOptIn at all'), and both feedback jobs pass `classification: "transactional"` -- the piggyback onto AC1's fixture is structurally sound.

No coverage gaps found. No case is vague or requires judgment to run. Independence confirmed: BACKEND-DEV's step-02 handoff committed no test file, so both designed files are genuinely new specifications, not a rubber stamp of already-existing tests.
